facts.title: A Sunday built from dots
facts.body: Seurat’s Grande Jatte (1884–86) freezes a Parisian island afternoon into pointillist stillness — leisure as a carefully composed science of color.

facts.title: Fashion at the right edge
facts.body: A woman with a bustle and a man in a top hat stand like statues of the bourgeoisie — modern types on parade.

facts.title: A pet with a leash
facts.body: A small monkey on a leash was a chic accessory — and a sly wink at “aping” social manners.

facts.title: Circles of shade
facts.body: Parasols punctuate the lawn like floating discs — fashion against the sun.

facts.title: The Seine as mirror
facts.body: Water beyond the bank holds boats and sky in cool fragments of color.

facts.title: Leisure on the water
facts.body: Sailboats and rowers echo the island’s Sunday ease — Paris at play.

facts.title: A child in white
facts.body: A young girl in a white dress holds flowers — innocence placed among rigid adults.

facts.title: Cool bands of shade
facts.body: Tree shadows stripe the grass — structure for Seurat’s dotted light.

facts.title: Color mixed in the eye
facts.body: Tiny strokes of pure color blend optically at a distance — pointillism’s wager on the viewer’s vision.
